/-!
# Erdős Problem 986

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
- [ChGr98] Chung, F. and Graham, R., *Erdős on Graphs: His Legacy of Unsolved Problems*.
  A K Peters, Ltd. (1998).
- [Br26] Bradač, D., Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers. arXiv:2605.28793 (2026).
- [Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.
- [MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraëte, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. Ann. of Math. (2024),
  941-965.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos986

/--
For any fixed $s\geq 3$,
$$R(s,k) \gg \frac{k^{s-1}}{(\log k)^c}$$
for some constant $c=c(s)>0$.

According to Chung and Graham [ChGr98] this was first conjectured by Erdős in 1947.

Proved by Bradač [Br26], with $c=2s-4$.

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) gives `k ^ (s - 1) / (log k) ^ c = O(R(s, k))`
for a natural `c > 0`, with the Ramsey number defined through `CliqueFree`/`IndepSetFree`; this
implies the statement below.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos986.lean#L92"]
theorem erdos_986 :
    ∀ (s : ℕ) (hs : 3 ≤ s),
      ∃ (c C : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
        ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in atTop,
          (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey s k : ℝ) ≥
            C * (k : ℝ) ^ (s - 1) / (Real.log k) ^ c := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos986

findings.description: The bibliography entry [MaVe23] at lines 29–30 gives the page range 941–965 for “The asymptotics of r(4,t)”. The published article occupies pages 919–941. This reference error does not affect the mathematical statement.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher’s article page states “Pages 919-941 from Volume 199 (2024), Issue 2”: https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2024/199-2/p08.

reformulations.difference: The file uses an explicit eventual lower bound with positive real constants and a Ramsey number defined by an infimum over complete-graph containment. The cited formal proof uses reverse big-O, a positive natural logarithmic exponent, and a Nat.find-based Ramsey number expressed using CliqueFree/IndepSetFree.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Complete-graph containment is equivalent to not being clique-free, and cliques in the complement are independent sets. Finite Ramsey’s theorem makes the defining set nonempty, so the two minimum constructions agree exactly. Eventual nonnegativity makes reverse big-O equivalent to the explicit positive lower-bound constant. Natural exponents embed into real exponents by Real.rpow_natCast; conversely, rounding a positive real exponent upward to its natural ceiling weakens the lower bound once log k ≥ 1. The full equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/bridge.lean; equivalence with the source’s Vinogradov notation was also proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the theorem. Its quantifiers, positive constants, exponent, and eventual bound match the source. Lean checks established nonemptiness of the Ramsey defining set, the harmless logarithm/division defaults at k = 0 and 1, and R(3,1) = 1 and R(3,2) = 3. The exact linked formal proof and its 32-module dependency closure compiled successfully; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The solved status agrees with the problem page and Bradač’s theorem. Full texts of the 1998 book and Spencer’s 1977 paper were unavailable; the problem page and Bradač’s primary paper explicitly state the conjecture and settle its interpretation.
